Light-controlled medicines, released exactly where they’re needed.

Welcome to the Pharmaceutical Chemistry & Drug Delivery Lab. We develop innovative strategies for drug discovery and delivery — for diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease — using pharmaceutical chemistry and photochemistry, guided by PK/PD modeling.

Core idea

What is photo-unclick chemistry?

Chemotherapy kills cancer cells — and healthy cells too. If a drug could stay inert everywhere except inside the tumor, side effects would fall sharply. Visible and near-IR light can reach deep tissue without the damage UV causes, but its energy is too low to break a bond directly. Photo-unclick solves that: light makes singlet oxygen, and singlet oxygen does the cutting.

1
Light on

A photosensitizer absorbs visible / near-IR light at the target site.

2
Singlet oxygen (¹O₂)

Energy transfers to oxygen. ¹O₂ lives ~40 ns and travels only ~20–200 nm — inherently local.

3
Linker cleaved, drug released

The β-aminoacrylate linker is cut by ¹O₂, freeing the active drug exactly there — and the released drug then overcomes ¹O₂’s short range with a bystander effect.

A singlet-oxygen-cleavable linker (center) is cut by light-generated ¹O₂, separating carrier from active drug. Illustration — see Research for schemes and primary papers.
